item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q012_not_true_family_specific_pair","answer":"Yes. In SCOPe 2.08, d1s9za_ is the 1s9z chain A domain under Protein node Amyloidogenic design-1, and d1hqja_ is the 1hqj chain A domain under Protein node Unnamed design-1; those two Protein nodes are different, but both domains have the same SCOPe family k.40.1.1, sunid 100905, Designed trimeric coiled-coil. Because their lowest shared node is a family, they also share the broader superfamily k.40.1, fold k.40, and class k, Designed proteins. The classification therefore supports homology at the SCOPe family level rather than only a weaker same-fold resemblance. The limit is that the shared family assignment should not be read as identity of construct, species node, bound ions or ligands: d1s9za_ is Amyloidogenic design-1 under its own Synthetic species node and is annotated as complexed with Na and Zn, while d1hqja_ is Unnamed design-1 under a different Synthetic species node and is annotated as complexed with Pb, sin, and SO4.","evidence_used":["compare_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1s9za_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1s9za_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1s9za_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1s9za_/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1hqja_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1hqja_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1hqja_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1hqja_/homology"]}]}
